title: Common Sense Media Reports Crisis Referrals Fell for ChatGPT for Teens
summary:
A dozen newly created accounts were able to discuss suicide and self-harm for up to an hour without notifying parents in a new safety audit. Common Sense Media tested 4,000+ prompts and found that crisis-safety metrics actually declined after the launch of the adolescent version of OpenAI's chatbot. Hotline referrals on matched crisis-level prompts dropped from 33% to 23%, professional referrals fell from 68% to 58%, and urgent-action language from 88% to 78%, with only four alerts received across the full test.

OpenAI disputes the methodology, stating that some tests may have occurred before parental controls fully activated. Common Sense replied that certain accounts stayed linked beyond the company's 3 hour activation window yet produced no alerts. These findings build on the group's earlier claims that the product is an "unacceptable risk" and its request that OpenAI block teenagers from the platform entirely because the bot continues to do schoolwork for minors.

selectedTweets.text:
This is disturbing: Common Sense says some crisis-safety metrics actually got WORSE after ChatGPT for Teens launched.

Researchers tested 4,000+ prompts. On more than a dozen newly created, parent-linked teen accounts, conversations about suic#de, self-harm or eating disorders lasted up to an HOUR without a single parental alert.

And on matched crisis-level prompts:

>hotline referrals: 33% → 23%
>professional referrals: 68% → 58%
>urgent-action language: 88% → 78%

Across the full crisis test, Common Sense received just four alerts.

The strangest part: the two post-launch alerts came from accounts with weeks of accumulated sensitive-topic history, not the newly created accounts used for acute crisis testing.

OpenAI disputes the methodology, saying some testing may have happened before parental controls fully activated.

Common Sense says some accounts remained linked beyond OpenAI’s roughly 3-hour activation window and still produced no alerts.
